candidate_relations.reason: Fibrolipoma is a localized lipomatous tumor, not congenital digit overgrowth of bone and fat.
Isolated neural lipofibromatous hamartoma is the related nerve lesion that the truncated label itself treats as excluded in favor of macrodystrophia lipomatosa.
Lipofibromatous hamartoma is a related fatty nerve hamartoma without the phalangeal overgrowth that defines MDL here.
Fibrolipomatous hamartoma is synonymous with LFH and remains a distinct entity from macrodystrophia lipomatosa.
Maffucci syndrome is a different overgrowth/vascular syndrome not described.
Macrodactyly is the parent digit-enlargement phenotype missing the lipomatous MDL identity.
Proteus syndrome is a related mosaic overgrowth syndrome with incompatible mosaic/systemic features not described in a single digit.
Macrodystrophia lipomatosa matches the reference diagnosis of congenital progressive lipomatous digit overgrowth.
Soft-tissue sarcoma is not suggested by lifelong enlargement with normal skin and lipomatous CT.
Lipomatous overgrowth is a parent tissue description missing the MDL digit diagnosis.
Hemihypertrophy is a broader regional overgrowth, incompatible with isolated middle-finger involvement.
Lipoblastoma is a different pediatric adipose tumor, not congenital phalangeal overgrowth.
Angiolipoma is a localized vascular lipomatous tumor, not MDL.
Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome is a vascular overgrowth syndrome; CT showed no abnormal vessels.
Neurofibroma is a different nerve tumor and does not explain bony phalangeal overgrowth.
Lipomatous macrodactyly is a conventional synonym for macrodystrophia lipomatosa of a digit.
Lipoma is a discrete adipose tumor, not congenital overgrowth of phalanges plus soft tissue.
Lipomatous tumor is a parent category missing the MDL phenotype.
Neurofibromatosis type 1 is a different overgrowth/tumor syndrome not described.
Neurofibromatosis is not supported by isolated congenital middle-finger lipomatous overgrowth.
